item.title: 'China, Thailand as close as one family' a unique advantage of bilateral ties, says Chinese premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
BANGKOK, Nov. 14 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Saturday that "China and Thailand are as close as one family" is a unique advantage of bilateral relations, as reflected in the practical achievements across various fields. Li made the remarks during his meeting with Thai King Maha Vajiralongkorn in Bangkok. Conveying cordial greetings from Chinese President Xi Jinping to the king, Li said that during the king's state visit to China last year, Xi held talks with him, and the two sides reached important consensus on advancing the building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future. China appreciates that the Thai royal family has long attached great importance to and remained committed to promoting China-Thailand friendship, Li said. He noted that the continued growth of China-Thailand economic and trade cooperation despite headwinds is particularly commendable amid the current turbulent international situation. Li said that China stands ready to work with Thailand, under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, to maintain close exchanges, expand cooperation in investment, technological innovation, new energy vehicles and other areas, deepen people-to-people exchanges, and promote economic and social development in both countries for the greater well-being of their peoples. The Thai king asked Li to convey his sincere greetings and best wishes to President Xi. Recalling his state visit to China last year, the king said that the successful meeting with Xi was fruitful and remained fresh in his memory. Li's official visit to Thailand would help further consolidate the traditional friendship between Thailand and China and deepen practical cooperation between the two countries, the king said.

item.title: Chinese premier lands in Manila for China-ASEAN summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
MANILA, Nov. 15 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang arrived in Manila on Sunday for the 29th China-ASEAN Summit at the invitation of President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr. of the Philippines, the rotating chair of ASEAN. Li arrived in the Philippine capital after concluding an official visit to Thailand and will attend the China-ASEAN Summit on Monday.

item.title: Xi's article on jointly building Asia-Pacific community with shared future to be published
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
BEIJING, Nov. 15 -- An article by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on jointly building an Asia-Pacific community with a shared future will be published on Monday. The article by Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, will be published in this year's 22nd issue of the Qiushi Journal, a flagship magazine of the CPC Central Committee. It is a compilation of excerpts from Xi's important remarks on the subject made between October 2013 and November 2025. The article stresses that the Asia-Pacific at present is an economic region with the world's greatest growth dynamism and development potential and is widely recognized as an important engine of global economic growth. It calls for sustaining the region's strong development momentum, embracing a future of shared prosperity, and jointly building an Asia-Pacific community with a shared future featuring openness and inclusiveness, innovation-driven growth, greater connectivity and mutually beneficial cooperation. The article points out that the Asia-Pacific should remain the locomotive of economic globalization. Efforts should be made to contribute significantly to the world through more vibrant and resilient Asia-Pacific cooperation, it notes. The article calls for taking the lead in safeguarding peace and stability, and resolving differences and disputes through dialogue and consultation. It emphasizes the need to play a leading role in enhancing openness and connectivity, firmly uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core, and advance regional economic integration and the building of the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific. The article also urges efforts to lead the way in pursuing win-win cooperation, fostering a pattern of cooperation in which countries support each other's success and achieve common development. It further underlines the importance of taking the lead in pursuing benefits for all and inclusiveness, with efforts to better bridge development gaps, continuously improve people's well-being, and advance common prosperity for all people in the Asia-Pacific. The article stresses that no matter how far China develops, it will remain rooted in the Asia-Pacific, contribute to its development and bring benefits to the region. China will remain committed to the path of peaceful development and pursue a win-win strategy of opening up. While pursuing its own development, China will actively promote common development among Asia-Pacific countries and create more opportunities for people in the region, it states. The article says China stands ready to work with all parties to jointly build an Asia-Pacific community, promote regional growth and prosperity, and advance practical cooperation in areas that include the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, connectivity, the digital economy and artificial intelligence.

item.title: China ready to deepen trade, economic exchanges with Thailand, says Chinese premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
BANGKOK, Nov. 14 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Saturday that China is ready to deepen trade and economic exchanges with Thailand and accelerate the construction of the China-Thailand railway. Li made the remarks during his talks with Sophon Zaram, president of Thailand's National Assembly and speaker of the House of Representatives. China encourages enterprises from both China and Thailand to cooperate in emerging sectors such as new energy and electronic information, strengthen collaborative innovation and jointly promote industrial upgrading, Li said. He said that in recent years, under the strategic guidance of Chinese President Xi Jinping and Thai King Maha Vajiralongkorn, China-Thailand relations have maintained steady and sound development, with fruitful cooperation across various fields. Last year, the two countries held grand celebrations marking the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations and the golden 50 years of China-Thailand friendship, Li said, noting that bilateral relations stand at a new historic starting point and face new development opportunities. Looking ahead, Li said, China is willing to work with Thailand to carry forward their traditional friendship, consolidate political mutual trust and make solid progress in building a China-Thailand community with a shared future, so as to bring greater benefits to the two peoples and better serve the modernization drive of both countries. The two sides should deepen exchanges and cooperation in areas such as culture, youth affairs, education and local affairs, enhance mutual understanding and friendship between the two peoples, and strengthen the public foundation of bilateral friendship, he said. Li said that the two sides should also strengthen coordination and cooperation in multilateral affairs to safeguard their common interests and international fairness and justice. He voiced hope that the legislative bodies of the two countries will strengthen exchanges and cooperation, support the implementation of major projects and practical cooperation, and play a greater role in providing legal guarantees and fostering closer people-to-people ties. For his part, Sophon said that Thailand and China enjoy a long-standing friendship and that Thailand deeply admires the remarkable development achievements made by the Chinese people under the leadership of the Communist Party of China. Thailand firmly adheres to the one-China policy and stands ready to work with China to maintain close high-level exchanges, advance exchanges and cooperation in areas such as connectivity, culture and education, law enforcement and security, and tourism, strengthen international coordination, and jointly address common challenges, Sophon said. The Thai parliament stands ready to provide a sound legal environment and safeguards for practical and mutually beneficial cooperation between the two countries to deliver more benefits to the two peoples, he said.

item.title: Xi stresses persevering with full, rigorous Party self-governance in state-owned enterprises
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
BEIJING, Nov. 13 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has emphasized the need to persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance in state-owned enterprises (SOEs) to provide strong guarantees for SOEs and state capital to get stronger, do better, and grow bigger. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction on Party building in SOEs. He noted that Party building in SOEs has been strengthened and new progress has been made across the board since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012. Xi urged further efforts to uphold and strengthen the Party's overall leadership of SOEs, better integrate the Party's leadership into all links of corporate governance, advance in-depth integration of Party building with production and operation, foster high-caliber, professional teams, and build good conduct, enforce discipline and fight corruption. The instruction was conveyed at a meeting on Party building in SOEs held in Beijing on Friday. Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and a member of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee, attended the event. Cai said Xi's important instruction has charted the course for further strengthening Party building in SOEs. Cai emphasized the need to accurately grasp the new requirements for Party building in SOEs arising from the evolving global, national and Party conditions. He called for efforts to resolutely combat corruption and further institutionalize and standardize the Party's leadership over SOEs.

item.title: Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, related events in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
BEIJING, Nov. 13 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and deliver remarks, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced Friday. The meeting will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19 under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the spokesperson said. The APEC CEO Summit will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 18 under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the spokesperson said, adding that President Xi will attend the opening ceremony and deliver a keynote speech. President Xi will hold a welcome banquet for participating leaders and representatives, and hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders on the sidelines of the meeting, the spokesperson added.

item.title: China holds gathering to mark 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
China holds gathering to mark 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth Updated: November 12, 2026 10:38Xinhua BEIJING, Nov. 12 -- China on Thursday held a gathering in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth. Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, addressed the gathering. Also present at the event were Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee. More than a century ago, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. He died in 1925.

item.title: Xi votes in local legislative election in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
BEIJING, Nov. 6 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping cast his ballot at a polling station in Beijing on Friday to elect deputies to a local people's congress. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, voted at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress. Xi stressed efforts to practice whole-process people's democracy, uphold Party leadership, and strengthen oversight throughout the election process to ensure that deputies who meet the people's expectations are elected. Around 3:30 p.m. Friday, Xi arrived at the polling station, gave his voter registration card to staff for verification, and got a ballot. He cast his ballot after filling it. Noting that the election of deputies to people's congresses is an important foundation for upholding, improving and practicing the people's congress system, Xi underlined the need to give full play to democracy, strictly act in accordance with the law, and ensure that the election is carried out fairly and cleanly. On Friday afternoon, other senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi cast their ballots in person, while Han Zheng entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Former Chinese leader Hu Jintao also entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Friday saw people vote at 13,054 polling stations across Beijing to elect 4,898 new deputies to the people's congresses at the district level and 11,137 deputies to the township-level people's congresses.

item.title: Chinese premier signs decree to revise, repeal certain administrative regulations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
BEIJING, Nov. 5 -- A decision by China's State Council to amend and repeal certain administrative regulations was made public on Thursday. Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree promulgating the decision, which aims to address pointless formalities to lighten the burden on those working on the ground, implement the reform of Party and state institutions, and ensure the consistency of relevant laws and regulations. Certain provisions of 14 administrative regulations were revised, and four regulations were repealed, according to the document. The State Council decided to revise a regulation on river course administration to align it with related provisions in the country's Ecological and Environmental Code. Meanwhile, a regulation on the limits of liability for maritime passenger transport between Chinese ports was repealed to better meet the needs of ongoing reform and development, and address practical realities in relevant areas. The decision takes effect on the date of its promulgation.
